changelog:
What you'll see with this update:
• Alert email now sends via a Gmail account (cytechalerts@gmail.com) instead of the old mail server -- live-tested delivering both the support copy and the owner copy.
• Config self-healing reliability fix: the automatic repair for a damaged settings file now runs on its own, independently of Home Assistant -- so it also works in the rare case where the file is too damaged for the system to start up normally (previously it could miss exactly that case).
• Update reliability: files now come from a version-pinned source, so an update can never half-install again (a unit could previously show the new version while still running old settings, and then refuse to re-apply).
• 'Config Check' row: the result shows just ok / restored / error / waiting -- no trailing number (it was an internal timestamp).
• The settings row 'Boots' is now 'Warnings' (in future it can carry alerts other than booting, too): it reads 'Repeated restarts' instead of the cryptic 'RESTART_STORM', with a plain-English message ('The unit restarted N times in the last 24h... please contact Cytech Support.'). The guard itself is unchanged: it flags 5+ restarts in 24h so Cytech can help.
• Config self-healing: if the main settings file is ever damaged, the unit repairs it from the last known-good copy and tells you (popup + email).
• A 'Config Check' row in the settings screen, refreshed right after every restart and every 4 hours.
• A clean alert-email setup: your address field is 'My Email for Alerts'; Register shows its result on screen; alerts always reach Cytech Support too, with your address copied automatically.
details:
v44 is the fleet-wide release of the bench-only 44a-44d fix revisions (previously staged as an aborted same-day 'v44' commit, immediately relabeled 44a since it wasn't ready for the fleet -- so this is the first time the plain '44' version/tag has actually shipped). What v44 ships:
(1) Config self-heal watcher now runs independently of HA Core: new ensure_config_integrity_watcher() in first_boot.sh (same pattern/de-dup approach as ensure_reset_watcher) runs cytech_integrity_check.py from inside the SSH addon container every 5 minutes, instead of only from a homeassistant.start-triggered automation. Fixes a real gap found by a live corruption test 2026-09-06: a configuration.yaml broken badly enough to fail parsing puts HA Core into Safe Mode, which does not load custom automations -- so the self-heal checker never ran in exactly the one case it exists for. Reproduced live (truncated configuration.yaml left the unit stuck in Safe Mode with no restore/alert/email); fixed and live-verified same day.
(2) Alert email moves from mail.server282.com (ucmapi@cytech.biz) to Gmail SMTP (cytechalerts@gmail.com). The old account was a single shared plaintext credential across the whole fleet with no per-device isolation or rotation path; Gmail App Passwords give each device its own revocable credential. cytech_email_gen.py's two notify platforms (cytech_alert_support, cytech_alert_email) now point at smtp.gmail.com, port 465/tls. Live-tested on the bench unit: both notify targets confirmed delivering, no SMTP/auth errors.
(3) New ensure_smtp_credential() in first_boot.sh distributes future SMTP credential rotations automatically: any device with CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN in .cytech_secrets fetches CY_SMTP_USER/CY_SMTP_PASS from a small private companion repo (ComfortHA-secrets, separate from this public one) via a read-only, single-repo, contents-only fine-grained PAT, and updates .cytech_secrets in place only if the values changed (idempotent -- a normal pass never restarts HA). Fetched from a private repo, not this one, because a public repo is scraped by credential-harvesting bots within minutes of a commit; if the fetch token itself leaks, the blast radius is limited to reading one small JSON file, not the SMTP password directly. Live-verified end-to-end on the bench unit.
CREDENTIAL CUTOVER, OPERATOR ACTION: the ucmapi@cytech.biz mailbox password is being rotated as part of this release, so it is no longer a working fallback for devices that haven't migrated. New devices get CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN baked in at provisioning and self-heal onto the new credential automatically. Already-fielded devices without the token will stop being able to send alert email until an operator adds CYTECH_SECRETS_TOKEN to that device's .cytech_secrets (over Remote Support Access or SSH) -- there is no bulk/automatic path for already-fielded units, so plan to migrate them opportunistically.
(4) 'Config Check' row shows just ok / restored / error / waiting -- no trailing epoch number.
(5) 'Boots' row renamed 'Warnings', with plain-English 'Repeated restarts' messaging (unchanged 5-restarts/24h guard).

v44 also carries everything v43 shipped (the fleet-wide release of the v42 series -- v42 plus fix-revisions 42a-42f, which only ever ran on the bench unit; 42a was an early rename-only attempt and 42d was a same-content re-ship for a delivery problem, so neither appears as a change below):
(1) CDN-proof downloads. raw.githubusercontent.com serves each URL from a CDN with max-age=300, keyed by the URL itself (a query string does NOT create a separate entry -- verified 2026-09-04), so a device downloading right after a release could be served the PREVIOUS version's file with no error, then write the new version label -- silently half-updated, and permanently unable to re-apply ('the units can never pull the real package, because the checker considers it up to date'). The bench unit hit exactly that during the 42c release. THE FIX: every release is git-tagged with its version and files are downloaded from the tag URL -- a URL no device has ever fetched, so it can never be served from cache. The manifest itself stays on the branch URL (stale reads there are harmless: 'up to date' for at most 5 minutes, then the next check is fresh). .cytech_secrets.example documents that CYTECH_MANIFEST_URL must not be pinned to a tag (the tag changes every release).
(2) cytech_integrity_check.py writes the status word only ('ok'), not 'ok <epoch>' -- the epoch leaked onto the Config Check dashboard row as an unexplained number.
(3) The boot guard state RESTART_STORM became REPEATED_RESTARTS with plain-English messages ('Repeated restarts detected' popup/email; message 'The unit restarted N times in the last 24h (first at HH:MM:SS local). Repeated restarts usually mean a problem -- please contact Cytech Support.'). Automation id cytech_alert_boot_storm is unchanged. (3b) The sensor 'Cytech Boot Status' is renamed 'Cytech Warning' -- the row is expected to carry other warnings besides boot/restart ones -- and its unique_id is bumped to cytech_warning_result_sensor on purpose: the entity registry pins an entity_id at first registration, so a name change alone would NOT move the id. A bumped unique_id re-registers every unit fresh as sensor.cytech_warning; units that already ran v35+ keep the orphaned sensor.cytech_boot_status (unreferenced, harmless). The on-disk result file (/config/.cytech_boot_result) and the dashboard row's message attribute are unchanged.
(4) The runtime integrity check also runs right after every core start (boot AND update restarts), not just every 4 hours, so the Config Check row shows its real result within minutes instead of 'unknown' for up to 4 hours after an update restart; before the first run ever it reads 'waiting' instead of HA's error-lookalike 'unknown'.
(5) Config self-healing: the system keeps a rolling known-good snapshot of configuration.yaml (refreshed after every clean check), and if the live file is ever found corrupt it is replaced by the snapshot with the broken copy saved as configuration.yaml.corrupt.<timestamp>, HA restarts, and the integrity alert says so. Two safety properties: the snapshot is only refreshed after the configuration actually parsed clean, so a corrupted state can never be snapshotted as 'good'; and no restore happens unless the snapshot itself parses, so there is no restore loop. Integrity alerts are emailed (support@cytech.biz always, plus the owner's registered address per the v41 rule), and the System Health dashboard shows a Config Check row with the last running check result. For v39 or older, v44 also carries v40 and v41: the owner's address field is 'My Email for Alerts', a Register press always reports its status on screen (empty field: 'Enter your email first, then press Register.'), a successful Register sends ONE confirmation mail To: the owner Cc: support@cytech.biz, alerts ALWAYS go to support@cytech.biz with the owner's registered address copied automatically (no Cytech/Me/Both selector), and units with mail configured but no owner registered yet show a small non-blocking hint. Nothing is lost if the owner never registers: support@cytech.biz always receives every alert.
